name: NeverFall sell() redeems protocol liquidity pro rata to the pair's spot NF balance
summary: NeverFall.sell(amount) removes amount * pairTotalSupply / balanceOf(pair) of the protocol-owned USDT/NF liquidity and pays the seller a share of the USDT. After flash-loaned USDT bought most of the NF out of the pair, the pair's NF balance was tiny, so selling NF removed almost all protocol liquidity and paid the attacker far more USDT than the NF was worth.

loss.notes: USDT that left protocol control: the attacker's net gain plus the 4,800 USDT flash-loan fee paid out of the proceeds. The 304,303.10 USDT routed to the protocol's own marketing wallet by the sell fee is not counted.

ageReset.description: Immutable NeverFallToken runtime; owner calls before the exploit are whitelist entries, test buys and setStartBuy, which open trading without changing the redemption formula.

sources.note: Loss. Root cause, anchor and age. Verified NeverFallToken source (Etherscan V2 getsourcecode, v0.8.18; SHA-256 of SourceCode 11ff0811afe5ebf9f840b032d6512f9857eae26cd5f90088f08f6be8c2905114): sell computes needLiquidity = amount * pair.totalSupply() / balanceOf(pair) and removes that protocol-owned liquidity, paying sellFee percent of the USDT out to the caller. Source-1 (block 27863178, index 3) buys NF with flash-loaned USDT, which drains the pair's NF balance, then sells NF back through sell(). SellNF(address,uint256,uint256) logs from deployment to block 27863178 show no other sale paying out more than 20,000 USDT; this one pays 1975353.99 USDT out of removed liquidity before fees. The DeFiHackLabs PoC (source-5) reproduces it. Age: eth_getCode is empty at block 26532686 and keccak256 of the runtime is the recorded hash at blocks 26532687 and 27863177; source-2 is a top-level creation by 0x051d6a5f987e4fc53b458ec4f88a104356e6995a at index 61. The contract has no upgrade path.
